card.name: Just before 'alone' in drug comparisons
card.fires_on: Words just before an expected 'alone' or 'used by itself', in sentences comparing a drug combination with one drug on its own. Also partway through hypoglycemia and drug names in combination-use passages.

modes.label: Comparison with single drug
modes.description: A linking word right before 'alone' when a combination is compared with one drug used by itself.
modes.example: lorazepam as compared to that observed<< with>> aripiprazole alone.

modes.label: Combination-use warnings
modes.description: Words inside interaction or combination statements, where the sentence is about drugs taken together.
modes.example: The concomitant use of ADDYI with multiple weak CYP3A4<< inhibitors>> may increase the risk of adverse reactions.

card.writes: It suppresses 'alone', 'solo' and 'single', so it steers the next word away from standalone wording.
card.plain: It fires in sentences about drugs taken together, just where a phrase like 'alone' might come next.
